info.title: Ambivo E-Sign & Contract Authoring API
info.description:
Native e-signature and contract authoring API for Ambivo CRM.

## Authentication
All `/user/*` and `/admin/*` endpoints require a Bearer JWT token in the `Authorization` header.
Public signing endpoints (`/esign/sign/*`) use a signing token in the URL path instead.

## Response Pattern
All JSON responses follow this convention:
- **Success**: `{ "result": 1, ...data }`
- **Error**: `{ "result": 2, "error": "message", "error_code": "CODE" }`

## A contract instance is a first-class entity

Since 2026-09, `contract_instance` is registered across the platform's generic
surfaces, so a contract carries the same capabilities as any other record and you do
NOT need an endpoint on this spec to reach them:

| Capability | How |
|---|---|
| Comments | `POST /user/comment/manage` with `entity_type: contracts` |
| Attachments | the platform attachment endpoints, same `entity_type` |
| List, filter, sort, search, export | `GET /entity/data?entity_type=contracts` |
| Charts and dashboards | the generic chart config for `contracts` |

⚠️ **The entity_type key is `contracts`, plural.** The class is `ContractInstance`
and the collection is `contract_instances`; all three differ. A request using
`contract_instance` matches nothing and is answered as an unsupported type.

Import is deliberately NOT wired: a contract is built from a template with merge
fields resolved and a signer list attached, and a spreadsheet row produces a document
bound to no template and addressed to nobody.

## Two Signing Modes

Both modes share the same signing engine (`NativeESignService`) and both start from
`draft` status. They differ in how the signing is set up:

| | Doc Sign (Direct) | Contract Sign (Template-Based) |
|---|---|---|
| **Initial status** | `draft` | `draft` (both start from draft) |
| **PDF source** | User uploads / provides HTML / selects file | Pre-uploaded on admin-managed template |
| **Template required** | No | Yes — must reference a `ContractTemplate` |
| **Signature fields** | Stored directly on the document | Defined on template, fetched at send time |
| **API steps** | 1–2 calls (create draft, then send) | 2–3 calls (create instance → preview → send) |
| **Status states** | 10 (draft, pending, sent, viewed, partially_signed, completed, declined, expired, cancelled, deleted) | 8 (draft, ready, sending, sent, signed, completed, cancelled, deleted) |
| **Is signing engine** | Yes — handles tokens, signatures, audit trail, PDF finalization | No — delegates to `NativeESignDocument` internally |
| **Admin governance** | No — users upload any PDF | Yes — admin controls available templates |
| **Entities** | `NativeESignDocument` | `ContractTemplate` → `ContractInstance` → `NativeESignDocument` |
| **Best for** | One-off documents, ad-hoc signing | Repeatable contracts with standardized PDFs |

**Contract Templates** are reusable signing packages: a PDF with pre-placed signature fields,
managed by admins. They provide standardized documents (users can't send the wrong version),
reusable field placement (no manual drag-and-drop each time), and governance (categories,
versioning, archival).

**Contract Instances** track each use of a template — who was sent what, linked to which CRM
entity (contact, opportunity), with what outcome. The instance copies the template's `pdf_url`
at creation time so existing instances are not affected if the template is later modified.

**Template Deletion:** Archiving (soft delete) is recommended. If a template is hard-deleted,
existing unsent instances may fail at send time because signature fields are fetched from the
template. Already-sent instances are fully independent.

The **Unified Documents** endpoint (`GET /user/documents`) merges both flows into a single
deduplicated list for display on CRM record pages.

## Creator-Fill Fields (Text Overlay)

Template signature fields support two modes based on `signer_index`:

| `signer_index` | Kind | Filled By | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| integer (0, 1, …) | **Signer field** | Signer during signing ceremony | At sign time |
| `null` | **Creator-fill field** | Contract creator at instance creation | Before sending — stamped onto PDF |

Creator-fill fields let the contract creator inject instance-specific text (e.g., party name,
designee) onto the PDF before signers ever see it. They must have `type: "text"` and a unique
`name` property (used as the key in `field_values`).

**Example template with both field types:**
```json
{
  "signature_fields": [
    {"id": "f1", "type": "text", "name": "party_name", "signer_index": null,
     "position": {"x": 30, "y": 15, "width": 40, "height": 3, "page": 1},
     "required": true, "label": "Party Name"},
    {"id": "f2", "type": "signature", "signer_index": 0,
     "position": {"x": 10, "y": 80, "width": 25, "height": 5, "page": 2},
     "required": true, "label": "Client Signature"}
  ]
}
```

**Instance creation with field values:**
```json
POST /user/contract/instance
{"contract_template_id": "...", "signers": [...],
 "field_values": {"party_name": "Acme Corporation"}}
```

At send time, `send_for_signature()` splits the template fields, overlays creator-fill values
onto the PDF, and passes only signer fields to the signing engine. Signers see a PDF with
"Acme Corporation" already printed — they just sign.

## Contract Authoring → Signing Flow

```
Step 1: Admin authors template
──────────────────────────────
Upload PDF           →  POST /user/file/upload
  or copy file       →  POST /admin/contract/template/copy-file
Create template      →  POST /admin/contract/template
  + signature_fields      signer fields:       {signer_index: 0, type: "signature", ...}
                          creator-fill fields:  {signer_index: null, type: "text", name: "party_name", ...}

Step 2: User creates contract instance
───────────────────────────────────────
Browse templates     →  GET /user/contract/templates
Create instance      →  POST /user/contract/instance
  + signers               [{email: "ceo@acme.com", name: "Jane Smith", role: "signer"}]
  + field_values           {"party_name": "Acme Corporation"}
                          → validated against template's creator-fill fields
                          → stored on ContractInstance

Step 3: User sends for signature
─────────────────────────────────
Preview (optional)   →  POST /user/contract/instance/{id}/preview
Send                 →  POST /user/contract/instance/{id}/send
                          1. Download PDF from S3
                          2. Split fields: creator-fill vs signer
                          3. Overlay field_values onto PDF (text at field positions)
                          4. Pass modified PDF + signer-only fields to NativeESignService
                          → NativeESignDocument created, signing emails sent

Step 4: Signer signs
─────────────────────
Open signing link    →  GET /esign/sign/{token}
                          Signer sees PDF with "Acme Corporation" pre-filled
                          Signer fills only their fields (signature, initials, date)
Submit               →  POST /esign/sign/{token}
                          → PDF finalized, audit trail recorded
```

## Endpoint Groups
- **Native E-Sign** - Create, send, and manage documents for signature (direct upload flow)
- **Public Signing** - Token-based endpoints for signers (no auth required)
- **Contract Templates** - Admin CRUD for reusable PDF templates with pre-placed signature fields
- **Contract Instances** - User flow for creating and sending contracts from templates
- **Unified Documents** - Combined listing of contracts and e-sign documents

---

## Compliance & Security

### Signature Standard

Ambivo Native E-Sign implements **Simple Electronic Signatures (SES)** — the most widely
accepted tier under both US and EU law.

| Standard | Supported | Notes |
|----------|-----------|-------|
| **ESIGN Act** (US, 15 U.S.C. § 7001) | Yes | Federal law; SES is legally equivalent to wet-ink for most commercial contracts |
| **UETA** (US, state-level) | Yes | Adopted in 49 states + DC |
| **eIDAS SES** (EU, Article 3(10)) | Yes | Admissible as evidence; cannot be denied legal effect solely because it is electronic |
| **eIDAS AES / QES** | No | Requires PKI certificates or qualified trust service providers — not in scope |

SES is the standard used by most e-signature platforms (including DocuSign, Zoho Sign,
HelloSign) for the vast majority of commercial contracts.

### Identity Verification & Authentication

| Control | Implementation |
|---------|----------------|
| **Email-based authentication** | Each signer receives a unique, cryptographically secure signing URL (`secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` — 256-bit entropy) |
| **Token expiry** | Signing links expire after 48 hours; sender can resend to generate a new token |
| **Optional access code (PIN)** | Sender can set a code per signer, communicated out-of-band. Signer must enter the code before viewing the document. Lockout after 5 failed attempts. |
| **Sequential signing** | When multiple signers are involved, each signer is only invited after the previous one completes |
| **Rate limiting** | All public signing endpoints are rate-limited per IP (5–20 req/min depending on endpoint) |

### Document Integrity & Tamper Detection

| Control | Implementation |
|---------|----------------|
| **Hash algorithm** | SHA-256 |
| **Original document hash** | Computed and stored at upload time |
| **Signed content hash** | Computed after signature overlay, proving integrity of the signed content independent of the certificate wrapper |
| **Signature hash** | Each signer's signature image is individually hashed and recorded in the audit trail |
| **Integrity verification** | On-demand API endpoint (`GET /user/native-esign/document/verify-integrity`) recomputes the hash from S3 and compares against the stored hash |
| **Tamper detection** | Any modification to the stored PDF produces a different hash, which the integrity check flags |

### Audit Trail

Every document maintains a **dual-layer audit trail**:

- **Layer 1 — Embedded in signed PDF**: Certificate of completion and full audit trail appended as pages in the signed PDF itself. The document is self-contained evidence.
- **Layer 2 — Queryable database records**: All events stored in a separate MongoDB collection with a 7-year TTL, queryable via API.

**Events captured**: document created, sent, viewed, signed, declined, completed, access code verified/failed, integrity check — each with timestamp, IP address, user agent, and geolocation (city/region/country).

**Per-signer data at signing**: full name, email, IP address, browser user agent, geographic location (resolved from IP), explicit electronic signature consent (boolean + timestamp), signature type (drawn/typed/uploaded) and image hash.

### Certificate of Completion

Every completed document includes an embedded certificate page containing: document name/ID, completion timestamp (UTC), original and signed content hashes (SHA-256), signer table (name, email, timestamp, IP, location), legal notice citing ESIGN Act and UETA, and full audit trail.

### Evidence Package Export

For completed documents, `GET /user/native-esign/document/evidence-package` returns a ZIP containing:

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `{name}_original.pdf` | Original unsigned PDF as uploaded |
| `{name}_signed.pdf` | Signed PDF with embedded signatures and certificate pages |
| `{name}_certificate.pdf` | Standalone certificate of completion |
| `audit_trail.json` | Machine-readable audit events with integrity verification result |
| `metadata.json` | Document metadata, signer details, hashes, timestamps, compliance info |

### Data Retention

| Item | Storage | Retention |
|------|---------|-----------|
| Signed & original PDFs | AWS S3 (encrypted at rest) | 10-year presigned URL expiry |
| Audit log records | MongoDB (separate collection) | 7-year TTL (auto-expiry) |
| Embedded audit trail | Inside signed PDF | Same as PDF retention |

tags.name: Contract Instances (User)
tags.description: User flow for contract creation and signing

tags.name: Unified Documents
tags.description: Unified document listing across contract instances and e-sign documents

tags.name: Audit Logs
tags.description:
Query audit trail for e-signature operations. Logs capture every lifecycle event
(created, sent, viewed, signed, declined, cancelled) with IP address, user agent,
and signer identity for legal compliance. Collection: `native_esign_audit_logs`
with 7-year TTL auto-expiry.

EntityType.description:
What a contract is linked to. `account`, `contact` and `opportunity` are the CRM
records a contract has always attached to; `order` is the sell-side order.

The last three are buy-side, added for the Procurement RFP award. A
contract awarded from an RFP points back at the `questionnaire` that
sourced it, the `purchase_requisition` that authorised the spend, and
the `purchase_order` that buys against it. Without them an award can
create the paperwork and cannot say what it came from.

See `POST /user/procurement/rfp/award` in the Procurement spec, which
is what creates a contract with `entity_type: questionnaire`.

WorkflowAction.description:
Action to execute when all signers have signed:
- `opportunity_close_won` - Move linked opportunity to Closed-Won stage
- `contact_customer` - Set linked contact status to "customer"
- `account_customer` - Set linked account status to "customer"
- `none` - No action

ContractInstanceStatus.description: `terminated` (since 2026-10-06): a fully signed contract ended early, kept on file with `terminated_ts`, `terminated_by_userid` and `termination_reason`. Set when an RFP award is revoked. `declined` (since 2026-10-07, question 43): a signer refused to sign, with `declined_ts`, `declined_by_email` and `decline_reason`. Set from the native e-sign decline and from the e-sign webhook, which mapped a decline to `cancelled` before. A declined contract cannot be cancelled; send a new one. When the contract came from an RFP award, the award is flagged for the buyer (ambivo-procurement spec, `POST /user/procurement/rfp/award`).

ContractInstanceAuditEventType.description:
Audit event types for contract instance lifecycle:
- `created` — Instance created from template
- `updated` — Instance details modified (signers, name, etc.)
- `sent` — Successfully sent for e-signature
- `send_failed` — Failed to send (with error details)
- `cancelled` — Instance cancelled by user
- `deleted` — Instance soft-deleted
- `restored` — Instance restored from deleted status
- `status_changed` — Status updated by esign document callback (e.g., signer signed)

AuditLogEntry.description: A single audit log entry for a native e-sign operation

audit_log_id.description: Unique audit log entry ID (MongoDB ObjectId)

native_esign_document_id.description: The e-sign document this event belongs to

event_data.description:
Event-specific metadata. Shape varies by event_type:
- **document_created**: `{document_name}`
- **document_sent**: `{signers: [{email, name, role}]}`
- **document_viewed**: `{signer}`
- **document_signed**: `{signer, signer_name, signature_hash, all_completed}`
- **document_declined**: `{signer, reason}`
- **document_cancelled**: `{}`
- **access_code_verified**: `{signer}`
- **access_code_failed**: `{signer, attempts_remaining}`
- **access_code_lockout**: `{signer}`

user_id.description: User ID who triggered the event (empty for public signer actions)

signer_index.description:
0-indexed signer reference, or null for creator-fill fields.
When null, the field is filled by the contract creator at instance
creation via `field_values` and overlaid onto the PDF before signers
see it. Creator-fill fields must have type "text" and a "name" property.

name.description:
Field name used as key in `field_values`. Required for creator-fill
fields (signer_index: null). Must be unique among creator-fill fields
in the same template.

access_code.description:
Optional access code/PIN that the signer must enter before viewing the document.
The sender communicates this code to the signer out-of-band (phone, SMS, etc.).
Max 5 failed attempts before lockout.

SignerResponse.description:
Signer details as returned in API responses. Note: the `access_code` value
is **never** included in responses for security. Use `has_access_code` to
check if an access code was set.

has_access_code.description:
Whether the sender set an access code/PIN for this signer.
The actual code value is never exposed in API responses.

access_code_verified.description: Whether the signer has successfully verified the access code

access_code_verified_ts.description: Unix timestamp when access code was verified

access_code_attempts.description: Number of access code verification attempts (lockout at 5)

signature_fields.description:
Signature field definitions from the source template. Included in
the detail response (`GET /user/contract/instance/{id}`) so the
editor can render field positions on the PDF preview. These are
not stored on the instance itself — they are looked up from the
template at request time.

pdf_url.description:
S3 presigned URL of the **original** template PDF (unsigned).
This is the PDF generated from the contract template with field values filled in.
Remains the same regardless of signing status.
10-year expiry, content-type `application/pdf`. Auto-regenerated from
`pdf_bucket`/`pdf_bucket_key` when expired.

signed_document_url.description:
S3 presigned URL of the **signed** PDF with embedded signatures,
certificate of completion, and audit trail.
Only populated after all signers complete and status reaches `completed`.
Empty string when not yet completed.
10-year expiry, auto-regenerated from stored S3 coordinates.

native_esign_document_id.description: Link to the NativeESignDocument created when contract is sent

field_values.description:
Creator-fill field values keyed by field name. These correspond to
template fields where `signer_index` is null. Values are overlaid
onto the PDF as text before the document is sent to signers.

audit_events.description:
Embedded audit trail for contract instance lifecycle events.
Records pre-send events (create, update, field changes) that cannot
be captured by the NativeESignDocument (which doesn't exist until send time).
Post-send events are also recorded here when the esign document triggers
status updates back to the contract instance.

esign_document_id.description: Linked esign document ID (for status_changed events)

UnifiedDocumentSource.description:
Indicates which system the document originated from:
- `contract` — Created via the contract template flow (ContractInstance)
- `esign` — Created directly via native e-sign (uploaded PDF, etc.)

UnifiedDocument.description:
A normalized document record returned by the unified listing endpoint.
Merges contract instances and standalone e-sign documents into a single shape.

status.description: Current status (uses the status enum of the source type)

pdf_url.description:
Smart PDF URL — returns the most relevant PDF for the document's current state.
When status is `completed`: the signed/finalized PDF (with embedded signatures and
certificate of completion). Otherwise: the original unsigned PDF (template PDF for
contracts, uploaded PDF for e-sign documents). All URLs are S3 presigned with 10-year
expiry, `ResponseContentType=application/pdf`, and `ResponseContentDisposition=inline`.

native_esign_document_id.description: Link to the NativeESignDocument (always set for esign source; set after send for contract source)

contract_instance_id.description: Contract instance ID (only for contract source)

post.description:
Create a new e-sign document in `draft` status without sending it.
Use this when you want to create the document first and send it later
via the `/send` endpoint.

signing_mode.description: Who gets a signing link and when. `sequential` notifies only the current order; `parallel` notifies every outstanding signer at once. An UNRECOGNISED value falls back to `sequential` rather than parallel, deliberately — the safe direction, so a typo cannot blast links to every party on a document whose author asked for a strict order.

source_id.description: Contract instance ID or file ID depending on source_type

custom_message.description: Custom message included in signing invitation email
custom_message.example: Please review and sign this agreement.

expires_days.description: Number of days before the signing link expires

example.custom_message: Please review and sign this service agreement.

put.description:
Update an existing e-sign document that is still in `draft` status.
All fields are optional — only provided fields will be modified.

Returns an error if the document is in any status other than `draft`.

signing_mode.description: Who gets a signing link and when. `sequential` notifies only the current order; `parallel` notifies every outstanding signer at once. An UNRECOGNISED value falls back to `sequential` rather than parallel, deliberately — the safe direction, so a typo cannot blast links to every party on a document whose author asked for a strict order.

native_esign_document_id.description: ID of the draft document to update

signers.description: Replacement signer list (replaces all existing signers)

custom_message.description: Updated custom message for signing invitation email

expires_days.description: New expiration days (recalculates expires_ts from now)

example.custom_message: Updated — please review the revised terms.

not_draft.summary: Document is not in draft status

value.error: Cannot update document in status: pending. Only draft documents can be updated.

post.description:
Supports two modes:
1. **Send existing draft**: Pass `native_esign_document_id` of a document created via `/document/create` (status must be `draft`)
2. **Create and send in one call**: Pass full document details (document_name, signers, etc.) to create and send in a single step

On send, the system:
- Generates secure signing tokens for each signer
- Sends email invitations with signing links
- Transitions document from `draft` → `pending` status

signing_mode.description: Who gets a signing link and when. `sequential` notifies only the current order; `parallel` notifies every outstanding signer at once. An UNRECOGNISED value falls back to `sequential` rather than parallel, deliberately — the safe direction, so a typo cannot blast links to every party on a document whose author asked for a strict order.

native_esign_document_id.description: For mode 1 - send an existing draft document

document_file_id.description: File ID of uploaded PDF document

create_and_send.summary: Create and send in one step

get.description:
Returns the current status, signer progress, and timestamps for a document.

Also returns `original_document_url`, `source_type`, `source_id`,
`workflow_action`, `custom_message`, `expires_days`, and
`signature_fields` (only for draft/pending documents — `null` otherwise).
These fields support the contract editor UI for rendering draft documents.

signed_document_url.description: S3 URL of signed PDF (only when status is `completed`)

original_document_url.description: S3 URL of the original unsigned PDF

custom_message.description: Custom message included in signing invitation email

expires_days.description: Number of days before the signing link expires

signature_fields.description:
Positioned signature field definitions. Only returned when
document status is `draft` or `pending` (for editor use).
`null` for all other statuses.

example.custom_message: Please review and sign this service agreement.

get.description: List e-sign documents with optional filters and pagination.

post.description: Cancel a document that has not yet been fully signed. All pending signing tokens are invalidated.

Soft delete a document that is in `draft` status. Sets the status to `deleted`.
The document can be restored back to `draft` via the restore endpoint.
Only draft documents can be deleted — documents in any other status must be cancelled instead.

delete_type.description: Indicates this was a soft delete — document remains in database with status "deleted" and can be restored.

400.description: Error (not in draft status or not found)

post.description:
Restore a soft-deleted document back to `draft` status.
Only documents in `deleted` status can be restored.

400.description: Error (not in deleted status or not found)

post.description:
Permanently remove a document from the database. This action cannot be undone.
Only documents in `deleted` status can be hard-deleted — soft-delete the document first.

delete_type.description: Indicates this was a hard delete — document permanently removed from database and cannot be recovered.

400.description: Error (not in deleted status or not found)

post.description: Resend the signing invitation email to a specific signer. Generates a new signing token.

post.summary: Resend the signing invitation, document unchanged
post.description:
Re-notifies the signers whose turn is **currently active** and regenerates
their signing links. It does not alter the contract, its signers or its PDF.

Only valid while the contract is `sent` or partially `signed`.

resent_to.description: Only the signers whose turn is active.

400.description: The contract is not in a resendable state

post.summary: Revoke a sent contract and reopen it for editing
post.description:
Invalidates **every** outstanding signing link on the linked e-sign document,
**voiding any signatures collected so far**, and returns the contract to an
editable state — `ready`, or `draft` if the PDF is no longer resolved.

⚠ The revoked e-sign document is **retained for audit**; sending again
creates a fresh one. Only valid while the contract is `sent` or partially
`signed`.

Prefer this over `POST /user/native-esign/document/revoke` for a contract
instance: that one kills the links but leaves the contract where it was.

400.description: The contract is not in a revocable state

post.summary: Revoke a sent document and void collected signatures
post.description:
Kills every signing link and **voids any signatures already collected**.

⚠ For a contract instance prefer `POST /user/contract/instance/{id}/revoke`,
which does this *and* reopens the contract for editing and resending. This
endpoint leaves the contract where it was.

400.description: The document is not in a revocable state

post.summary: Resend invitations to every signer whose turn is active
post.description: "Active" is decided by the document's `signing_mode`: under `sequential` that is the current order only, under `parallel` it is every outstanding signer.

400.description: Nothing to resend, or the document is not sent

get.summary: The signing links for a document's active signers

post.summary: Copy a file into a StoredFile ready to be signed
post.description:
Takes a file from an existing tenant file, Google Drive or Microsoft Drive and
produces a new `StoredFile` usable as the document PDF.

**One of three source shapes:**

- `{"source": "existing_file", "file_id": "..."}`
- `{"source": "google_drive", "provider_file_id": "...", "email": "..."}`
- `{"source": "microsoft_drive", "provider_file_id": "...", "email": "..."}`

The `email` identifies which connected drive account to read through.

provider_file_id.description: The drive's own file id, for the two drive sources.

email.description: Which connected drive account to read through.

400.description: Unknown source, or the file could not be read

post.summary: Re-email the signed copy to the signer on file (public)
post.description:
**Public** — the signing token is the authorization; no bearer token.

Powers the "Email me the signed copy" button on the Already Signed page.

⚠ **The document is only ever sent to the email already on file for that
token.** The caller cannot name a recipient, so a leaked link cannot be used
to forward a signed contract somewhere else.

Rate limited: 5 requests per 5 minutes, per IP for unauthenticated callers.

200.description: Queued to the signer on file

get.description:
Get available workflow actions that can be triggered on document completion.
Optionally filter by entity type to get only relevant actions.

parameters.name: entity_type
parameters.description: Filter actions relevant to this entity type

get.description:
Public endpoint that renders the HTML signing page for a signer.
The signing token serves as authentication. No Bearer token required.

The page includes:
- Document PDF viewer
- Signature capture (draw, type, or upload)
- Electronic disclosure consent
- Submit and decline buttons

If the signer has an `access_code` set by the sender and not yet verified,
the page renders an access code input screen instead. After successful
verification via `POST /esign/sign/{token}/verify-code`, reloading
this page renders the normal signing page.

Rate limited to 20 requests per minute per IP.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Signing token received via email

post.description:
Record that the signer has viewed the document.
Called automatically when the signing page loads.
Updates the signer status to `viewed` and records the view timestamp.

Submit a signature for the document. Requires explicit consent to the
electronic signature disclosure (ESIGN Act compliance).

After submission:
- If more signers remain, the next signer receives their invitation
- If all signers are done, the document moves to `completed` status,
  the signed PDF is generated, and any workflow action executes
- If the document originated from a contract instance, the signer statuses
  are synced back to the contract instance and an audit event is recorded

consent_given.description: Must be `true` - signer consents to electronic signature

post.description:
Decline to sign the document. The document status is set to `declined`
and the document sender is notified via email.

Verify the sender-set access code/PIN before allowing document access.
Rate limited to 5 requests per minute per IP.
After 5 failed attempts, the signer is locked out and must contact the sender.

code.description: Access code/PIN set by the document sender

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive search by template name (substring match)

parameters.name: include_fields
parameters.description: Include signature_fields arrays

post.description:
Create a new contract template with optional PDF and signature fields.
Upload the PDF first via `/user/file/upload`, then reference it by `pdf_file_id`.

pdf_hash.description: Hash of the source PDF, stored with the template. A later verify-integrity check compares against it, so a template whose PDF was swapped underneath can be told from one that was not.

delete.description:
Soft-delete by setting `is_active` to false. Archived templates no longer appear
in user-facing template lists but remain in the database.

**Impact on existing instances:**
- **Already-sent instances**: Fully independent — they have their own PDF URL (copied at creation) and the NativeESignDocument has its own copy of signature fields.
- **Unsent draft instances**: The `send_for_signature()` method fetches `signature_fields` from the template at send time. If the template is archived, it can still be looked up internally. If hard-deleted, the send will fail.

**Recommendation:** Always use archive (this endpoint) instead of hard delete to preserve template data for existing instances.

Copy a PDF from an existing tenant file, Google Drive, or Microsoft Drive to create
a new StoredFile ready for use as a contract template PDF.

This is a surrogate to the manual upload flow (`POST /user/file_upload`). Instead of
uploading a PDF, users can reference an existing file or pull one from a connected
cloud drive. The resulting StoredFile has `entity_type='contract_template'` and
`is_draft=True`, and its `file_id` can be passed to `POST /admin/contract/template`.

**Supported sources:**
- `existing_file` — Copy from a PDF already stored in the tenant's files
- `google_drive` — Download/export a file from a connected Google Drive account
- `microsoft_drive` — Download/export a file from a connected Microsoft OneDrive account

Google Docs and Microsoft Office files are automatically exported to PDF.
Non-PDF, non-exportable files are rejected.

get.description:
Unified document listing that merges contract instances and native e-sign
documents into a single deduplicated list.

**Default behavior:** Documents with status `deleted` are excluded by default.
Pass `include_deleted=true` to include them.

**Deduplication rule:** When a contract instance has been sent and has a
linked `native_esign_document_id`, only the contract instance appears in the
results (it represents both entities). Standalone e-sign documents (uploaded
directly, not originating from a contract) appear separately.

Each document includes a `source` field (`"contract"` or `"esign"`) so the
frontend can determine which detail endpoint to call for full info.

**Security:** Signer `access_code` values are stripped from responses.
Only `has_access_code` (boolean) is included.

get.summary: Get audit log entries for a specific e-sign document
get.description:
Returns the full audit trail for a native e-sign document, ordered by
timestamp descending (most recent first).

Each entry captures a lifecycle event with metadata:
- **Who**: `user_id`, `signer_email`
- **What**: `event_type`, `event_data`
- **When**: `timestamp` (epoch seconds)
- **Where**: `ip_address`, `user_agent`

### Event Types
| event_type | Trigger |
|---|---|
| `document_created` | Document created as draft |
| `document_updated` | Draft document modified |
| `document_sent` | Sent for signature (includes signer list in event_data) |
| `document_viewed` | Signer opened the signing page |
| `document_signed` | Signer submitted their signature |
| `document_declined` | Signer declined to sign (includes reason in event_data) |
| `document_cancelled` | Sender cancelled the document |
| `access_code_verified` | Signer successfully verified their access code |
| `access_code_failed` | Signer entered wrong access code (includes attempts_remaining) |
| `access_code_lockout` | Signer locked out after 5 failed access code attempts |

### Access Control
Requires authentication. Results are scoped to the current user's tenant.

### Collection & Indexes
Collection: `native_esign_audit_logs`
- Index: `{native_esign_document_id: 1, timestamp: -1}` — optimizes this query
- TTL: 7-year auto-expiry on `timestamp` field

parameters.description: Records per page (max 200)

get.description:
Query audit log entries across all e-sign documents for the tenant.
Supports filtering by event type, signer email, and time range.

Results are ordered by timestamp descending (most recent first).

### Filtering

All filters are optional and can be combined:

| Filter | Index Used | Use Case |
|---|---|---|
| (none) | `{tenant_id, timestamp}` | All tenant audit logs |
| `signer_email` | `{signer_email, timestamp}` (sparse) | Activity for a specific signer |
| `event_type` | `{tenant_id, timestamp}` | All signing events, all views, etc. |
| `start_ts` + `end_ts` | `{tenant_id, timestamp}` | Events within a date range |

### Access Control
Requires authentication. Results are scoped to the current user's tenant.

### Time Range
Use `start_ts` and `end_ts` (epoch seconds) for date range filtering.
Both are optional — use just one for open-ended ranges.
